content.summary_of_the_paper: In this work, the authors mainly focus on the few-shot key point detection problem. They propose a modified ViT based model, adding the saliency maps as additional soft masks to distinguish the foreground and background. The experimental results the effectiveness of their proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The paper is easy to follow. Will the authors release the codes and models for this community? If yes, it would be much better and helpful. 

However, there exist the following concerns to prevent me vote for acceptance. 

Firstly, the authors might fail to clearly explain the motivations for this work. For example, from the first sentence in the abstract, the readers might confuse to understand how the long-range dependency could help improve few-shot keypoint detection, or only for this task, or for more general tasks including semantic segmentation, not only the few-shot setting. Besides, the long-range dependency has been studied recently, such as non-local tech or dynamic conv.  Why not use them? In other words, the authors might focus on how to use one specific tech, saliency or soft masks, on one specific task, i.e., the few-shot keypoint detection, which is more suitable for vision conferences. 

Then, the main contributions include the masked self-attention and morphology learner. As for the used saliency maps, it’s interesting to involve the predicted saliency from the current method, which might be more accurate. However, at the same time, it would also bring more costs and the performance would depend on the used saliency model, which limits the generalizability of the proposed model. Besides, the idea of attention is commonly used in recent years, which might not be a significant contribution. 

Finally, the authors might need to add more ablation studies, to indicate the motivation, such as why not to use CNN, with non-local, dynamic conv, or other transformers. 

Minors. The authors might need to refine their paper and the writing might be further improved.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is easy to follow. But this work might lack novelty. The authors provide a detailed implementation for reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: Considering the three concerns of weakness, I vote for rejection.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a saliency-guided vision transformer SalVit for few shot keypoint detection. A saliency map is used as soft mask to constrain the self-attention of ViT to foregrounds while a morphology learner adjusting the morphology of the saliency map. The ViT feature is used together with CNN features to provide a more informative representation. The authors apply SalViT in the inductive and transductive settings for few shot keypoint detection, and show that it outperforms previous approaches.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. The authors provide extensive experiments results to show the effect of each component of the proposed method. The proposed method is compared to five previous methods on three benchmark datasets and demonstrates better performance. 
2. The paper is readable. The figures clearly demonstrates the idea and the overall framework. 
3. It is reasonable to constrain self-attention in foreground region for keypoint detection. 

Weakness:
1. The novelty is limited. Saliency has already been used in improving self-attention [a] and in few shot learning tasks [b]. The use of saliency in this work seems to be very similar to [a]. Both use the saliency scores to modulate the attention weights. 
[a] Saliency-Guided Attention Network for Image-Sentence Matching. Zhong et al. ICCV 2019.
[b] Boosting Few-shot visual recognition via saliency-guided complementary attention. Zhao et al. Neurocomputing. 
2. The saliency detection model is trained on an external dataset, which many include the novel species. This could potentially break the few-shot setting and lead to unfair comparison. 
3. The performance seems to be very sensitive to the saliency detection model according to Table 5. In some cases the saliency detection model may harm the keypoint detection performance, e.g. when detecting keypoints of a non-salient objects, such as a camouflage object that has similar appearance to the background. 
6. Some implementation details are not clear. E.g. the morphology operator $()^{\theta \downarrow}$ in (8) is undefined. 
5. The scope of this paper might be too limited. It only applies to vision transformer and only for the keypoint detection task in the few shot setting. It is likely to be of limited interest to the machine learning community.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is readable and the quality of the figures are satisfactory. However, the novelty seems to be limited. Some implementation details are missing.
content.summary_of_the_review: Considering the limited novelty and scope, I think the weakness outweigh the strength. There are also other minor issues discussed in the Strength and Weaknesses section.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work's writing is straightforward, and its methodology is intuitive. When it comes to the task of few-shot keypoint detection, cutting-edge results are attained.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
+ Writing is good.
+ SalViT achieves SoTA performance in few-shot settings.
+ The approach itself is intuitive and predictably effective.

Weaknesses
- What concerns me is that the concept of creating mask regions in a salient region or part of the target body has been mentioned several times in articles, particularly in the derivative versions of VIT and MAE. Except for the detailed benchmarks, the authors do not mention the relevant work or explain the difference. So the novelty of M-SA is questioned.
- This work may be limited to simple images (that have few semantics). However, the reviewer suggests responding positively to this question by stating in the introduction section that it has special advantages in many certain scenarios. The authors can consider e-commerce scenarios [1], where the main part and key points are beneficial in the e-commerce field.
- The ablation experiments are not described in great detail. There are not many noteworthy parts, particularly similar PE, Mask Ratio, and modified SA has appeared numerous times in recent research.
- Interpretable visualizations are really important for this paper but they are missing.

[1] Kaleido-BERT: Vision-Language Pre-training on Fashion Domain (CVPR2021)
content.summary_of_the_review: The reviewer thought this was a moderate article, and I am satisfied with the narrative parts (introduction and architecture), the authors write in a good way. But the experiments and ablation experiments, which only proved useful for components but did not throw many very insightful points, making the introduction part somewhat overclaimed.

content.title: Saliency-guided Vision Transformer for Few-shot Keypoint Detection
content.abstract: One attractive property of Vision Transformer (ViT) is to capture long-range dependency among image patches, which helps improve few-shot keypoint detection (FSKD) and is not explored yet in the literature. However, the simple application of ViT brings in irrelevant features outside of the region of interest due to the global attention matrix, thus degrading similarity learning between support and query features. In this paper, we present a novel saliency-guided vision transformer, dubbed \emph{SalViT}, for few-shot keypoint detection. Our SalViT enjoys a uniquely designed masked self-attention and a morphology learner, where the former introduces saliency map as a soft mask into ViT and constrains the self-attention to foregrounds, while the latter leverages the so-called power normalization adjusting morphology of saliency map, realizing dynamically changing receptive field. With the SalViT, we explore the use of ViT features together with CNN features to model both local and long-range dependency, providing more informative representations for similarity learning. We apply SalViT to FSKD in inductive and transductive settings, and show that it outperforms other methods.
